full_judgment: 2. The present leave-petitioners and the predecessors of the respondent Nos. 18 to 26 and the respondent No. 27, as plaintiffs, filed Title Suit No. 388 of 1976 in the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Comilla for declaration of their title in the suit land. The said suit was subsequently transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Comilla and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 177 of 1979. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, was that the land of plot Nos. 106, 105. 106/524 belonged to Tripura Moharaja. That the said Moharaja settled the said land described in schedule No. 1 to the plaint to sree Nibaran chandra Ganguli on 19.10.1942. The said landlord settled the land of schedule No. 2 also to Sree Nibaran Chandra Ganguli as per rule 72 of Wards Mannual Act. 1930 and rule 24 of Crown Estate Mannual, 1932. That Sree Nibaran Chandra Ganguli got possession of the said land and possessed the same. He also constructed a shop of 24 doors in the suit land and let out those to different persons. He also excavated a big pond in the suit land and used to cultivate fish in that pond. That the government requisitioned that 24 doors shops vide Requisition Case Nos. 89 of 1947 and 249 of 1948 and allotted those to non-Bengali Moharaja and Fishery Department. That Nibaran Chandra Ganguli died leaving behind four sons, namely, Mahendro Chandra Ganguli, Nirod Chandra Ganguli, Nirmal Chandra Ganguli and Nipendra Chandra Ganguli @ Tutu Ganguli and through amicable partition Nirod Chandra Ganguli, Nirmal Chandra Ganguli and Nipendra Chandra Ganguli got the suit land in their saham. In the first part of 1964 the said three owners of the suit land decided to exchange the suit land with the Indian property of the plaintiff Nos. 1, 2 and 3 for that purpose a provisional power of attorney was executed, but since the same was not done as per law the same was cancelled and on 17.04.1964 the said 3 brothers appointed one Ali Mia as their constituted attorney. The said attorney, by filling Miscellaneous Case No. 1379 of 1965/66 obtained permission on 26.06.1967 from the proper authority and thereafter by observing all the legal formalities registered an ewajnama in favour of the plaintiff Nos. 1-3. That the shops and the lands which were requisitioned were subsequently derequisitioned infavour of the original owner. But taking the advantage of wrong recording of the suit land the defendant Nos. 1-3 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 1967-68 under Bengal Tenancy Act and illegality delivered possession of the suit land to Fishery Department. But subsequently on finding title and possession of the plaintiffs those land were returned to the plaintiffs. That the defendant No. 4 and others gave threat to the plaintiff Nos. 1-3 not to cultivate fish in the pond of the suit land and in that situation the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 41 of 1973 for permanent injunction which was subsequently withdrawn on the ground of formal defect with permission to sue afresh. Another suit being No. 163 of 1969 was filed by the plaintiffs, but subsequently the same also was withdrawn with permission to sue afresh. Since the suit land was not recorded in the name of the plaintiff Nos. 1-3, the defendants were trying to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land and also took initiative to settle the suit land to different persons which compelled the plaintiffs to file the instant suit.
